'''''Limonium ramosissimum''''', the '''Algerian sea lavender''', is a species of sea lavender (''[[Limonium]]'') native to the [[Mediterranean region]].
Its [[botanical name|specific epithet]] {{lang|la|[[wikt:ramosissimus|rāmōsissimum]]}} means "many-branched" in Latin.

==Ecological characteristics==
As a [[halophyte]], ''Limonium ramosissimum'' has the ability to tolerate a wide range of salt levels ([[salinity-tolerant]]) in the soil and also has the ability to actively lower the [[soil salinity]] by taking up and excreting salt through glands in the [[inflorescence]], which are then free to [[abscission#In plants|break off]] and blow away.<ref name="Presentation. Society of Wetland Scientists Conference, Sacramento, CA.">{{cite journal|last=Page|first=M|author2=Schroeder, S. |title=Ecology of the Exotic Sea Lavender ''Limonium ramosissimum'' in the salt marshes of southern California|year=2007}}</ref> This could have the effect of changing the [[species composition]] of an area by reducing salinity in the soil.

===Invasive species===
These plants are also very fecund, producing many seeds, and are also able to compete with native flora. It has [[escaped plant|escaped cultivation]] and become an [[invasive species]] in [[salt marshes]] of California.<ref>{{cite web|title=CalFlora: Limonium ramosissimum |url=https://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=9147|publisher=CalFlora|access-date=24 November 2010}}</ref>
